advisor-model: Owner 2026-11-06: Fable only as the advisor (second opinion on approach), never as a subagent for reviews, captures or checks. Scoped small tasks (reviews, captures, triage, mechanical fixes) go to Sonnet or Haiku subagents; Opus only for design or risky changes. Supersedes the per-screen Fable design-review exception.
android-release-key: private/android-signing/digitva-release-20261019.* is the OLD 0.1.0 key (cert 1E60B3C0...); its certificate-sha256.txt matches the old key, so checking against it proves nothing. Release key is CI-only (env android-release, cert 6D94718A..., docs/current-state/android-release-builds.md). Verify APKs against that doc. A wrong-key APK fails INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE and uninstalling deletes unsent work (2026-10-27).
builds-on-ci-only: Owner 2026-10-25: no local APK or Expo web-export builds on the Mac for release or distribution; release builds only on GitHub Actions (android-release.yml, server-images.yml, web-export and Collect Plus workflows). Owner 2026-10-29 exception: local DEBUG dev builds with Metro/HMR (npm run android:plus:dev) are allowed for development and emulator screenshots; they are never distributed. The 2026-10-26 hold on publishing the engine bundle was lifted 2026-10-29 on condition that all inputs are public and unrestricted (see who-icd11-offline-permission).
code-writer-model: Owner 2026-11-06: code-writer model by complexity: Haiku wherever possible, Sonnet for intermediate work, Opus only for design decisions and broad/risky changes. Codex counterparts: Opus=Sol, Sonnet=Terra, Haiku=Luna. Supersedes the 2026-10-24 Haiku-writer rule.
coder-phone-ram: Owner 2026-10-24: coders' phones have at least 6 GB RAM. The test Samsung SM-E146B (6 GB model, MemTotal 5.3 GB) is representative for Collect Plus offline ICD-11/DORIS memory profiling.
coding-parity-all-surfaces: Owner 2026-10-30: the coding process must work the same way on the web, Collect (online coding) and Collect Plus (online and offline): same case data review (categories, positive/negative history, symptom summary, narrative), same certificate/DORIS/CoDEdit flow and checks. Offline is not a reduced mode. NQA and Social Autopsy follow the project setting online and for enrolled accounts; in standalone mode both NQA and SA are disabled. Tracked in digitva-9cll.22.
collect-theme-direction: Owner 2026-11-05: Collect theme direction = Petrol primary #1f4d60 (oklch 39.7% 0.059 228) + amber accent #d6a24a with ink text on accent; canvas #e8edf0, white cards with NO borders (tone + faint shadow; inset hairline separators; selected/error = tint fill), dark mode derived (primary #6fb6d6). Native icons: SF Symbols on iOS (expo-symbols), Material Symbols on Android, same meanings. Mockups in session scratchpad theme/petrol.py. Not yet approved to build.
commit-file-filter-bsd-grep: BSD grep on this Mac ignores \| in basic regex, so grep -v '^mobile/\|^vendor/' excludes nothing (2026-10-05 it swept Expo files into backend commit eeec15eb). Build commit lists with grep -Ev '^(mobile|vendor)/' and check git diff --cached --name-only | grep -E '^(mobile|vendor)/' is empty before committing.
commit-timing-owner-decides: Owner 2026-10-14: do not commit until the owner says so, and do not keep asking. Prefer one larger commit over several small ones. Finish, review, test, report ready, then stop.
coordinator-role: Owner 2026-10-23/11-04: the main session is the coordinator. It delegates as it judges fit, one worker per task/files/test DB, stops duplicate forks (keeps the one further along), and when a committer session owns landing it relays each ready change (branch, commit, exact test counts, changelog/handoff lines) to the committer; children never push main.
dev-webauthn-rp: Dev passkeys need WEBAUTHN_RP_ID=localhost and WEBAUTHN_ORIGIN=http://localhost:8051 (set in docker-compose.override.yml): dev .env carries the production MAIL_BASE_URL, from which the RP is otherwise derived. End-to-end passkey check: Playwright + CDP WebAuthn.addVirtualAuthenticator against localhost:8051 (Chromium from ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright).
doris-engine-version: Owner 2026-10-25: stay on DorisRuleEngine 1.1.176 (whoicd/icd-api:2.6.0, DLL sha256 c3c17cf1...) on server and Collect Plus alike; move both to 1.2.1 only when WHO ships it in an official ICD-API image. 10,010-case suite: server 1.1.176 matched the 1.2.1 reference on cause/URI/reject/report/errors for all cases (2026-10-25).
handoff-per-step: Owner 2026-10-02: during multi-step work, update handoff.md in the working tree as each step completes, but do not make a separate commit for each handoff update; it goes in with the next real commit or at session end.
icd11-android-bridge-primary: Owner 2026-10-29: the Android bridge (mobile/digitva-collect/modules/digitva-icd11: NativeAOT libdigitva_icd11.so, Bridge.cs, shim.c, Kotlin service) is the primary ICD-11/DORIS use case, and the phone must do the whole web DORIS coding flow completely offline (search with badges, Use, Build, details, hierarchy, maternal/perinatal related, axes and postcoordination options, selection check, DORIS, CoDEdit, UCOD, rules, errors, VA definitions, allowability, save) with no server call. The desktop station's Rust host (vendor/who-icd11-api, desktop/) is secondary and not for Android; the server keeps WHO's container for online coding.
icd11-server-container: Owner 2026-10-26: servers (staging, production) use the official WHO whoicd/icd-api Docker image permanently; this is settled and matches WHO's advice (call the API endpoints). The Rust ICD host (digitva-icd11-server) is not a server path; offline in-process engines (PHC desktop, Collect Plus) remain the only open licensing question (see who-icd11-offline-permission).
ldh-manuscript-master: Owner 2026-11-07: the LDH manuscript and appendix are edited on Google Drive only (folder 'DigitVA Platform Paper': manuscript 1O2cFwZqgyZ7sh87VkjiYgHQ8oM2Diuho, appendix 12UMIGl0DrIIYtLNA0ZVVPk22u0n7OPMd). docs/manuscript/*.docx and scripts/build_digitva_ldh_manuscript.py are stale; never rebuild over Drive. To make an edit: rclone backend copyid gdrive: <id> <file> to fetch, edit with python-docx (keep Zotero fields), then rclone copyto to the same Drive path (same ID; Drive keeps versions). The Drive MCP connector is denied in .claude/settings.local.json; use rclone (remote gdrive:).
medical-records-named-extension: Medical records IS a named extension. Decided by the owner 2026-09-19 for digitva-thr (corrects an earlier mis-note in this same key). A 'medical_records' identifier joins enabled_extensions, which becomes eight names: digitva_core, social_autopsy, intake_screen, geography, narration_language, death_summary, medical_records, abha. The md_available / md_count / md_im1..30 fields move OUT of digitva_core, which had carried them in the canonical table in docs/policy/va-form-project-configuration.md; that table and the Tier-1 list plus derivation rule in docs/policy/va-web-form-options.md must be updated. md_available does not exist yet in vendor/who-va-2022/src/digitva-extension.ts and must be authored; md_count and md_im1..30 exist there but are spliced in unconditionally by instrument.ts and must become conditional on the layer. Mirrors death_summary, whose fields are likewise ungated today.
migration-tests-are-slow: Do not give writers or runners the whole tests/migrations directory: each test builds a fresh database and replays the migration chain, so the directory takes far longer than tests/routes + tests/services (~80 s). Run only the new migration's test plus tests/migrations/test_schema_drift.py and test_no_app_imports_in_migrations.py (and the neighbouring migration's test if it shares tables).
no-db-bomb-probes: 2026-10-27: a security reviewer crashed shared dev Postgres twice with a memory-bomb probe (repeat('a',900000000)). Every reviewer/writer brief touching SQL sandboxes must forbid executing memory/CPU/disk/lock bomb SQL on any DB; test validators in Python only, or caps with small safe inputs.
no-fable: Owner 2026-11-06: no Fable subagents (weekly usage). Fable only as the advisor tool. Sonnet/Haiku for reviews, captures, triage and small fixes; Opus only for design or risky changes.
no-legacy-fallbacks: Owner 2026-10-05: the field-collection work (answers hash, drafts sync, revisions, served form, notifications) is not deployed anywhere yet; do not add backfills or legacy-row fallbacks for data created by this unreleased work.
no-per-code-icd-11-coding-policy-json: No per-code ICD-11 coding policy JSON exists on any branch (verified 2026-09-19: main, origin/icd-11, claude/*). The curated source is docs/icd-causegrp-mappings/ICD-to-VA-Buckets/who_2022_va_cause_list_icd10_icd11.csv (WHO 2026 annex ranges per VA cause); the policy is generated from it for the owner's review, with specific-code-beats-range and a separate scheme JSON, as for ICD-10.
owner-decision-2026-10-20-outside-self-c: Owner decision 2026-10-20: outside self-coding projects, coders must be blocked from coding (random or pick) VAs they collected themselves; self-coding projects keep digitva-xuxk behaviour. Tracked in digitva-yeg3.1.
owner-decision-2026-10-20-the-coder-reco: Owner decision 2026-10-20: the coder recode/review window (hard-coded 24h) becomes a per-project setting, default 24h, with deadline shown in My coded cases. Tracked in digitva-yeg3.2.
perf-first: Owner 2026-10-04: code must be extremely fast and efficient. Every writer brief: index-backed queries, no N+1, no per-row queries in lists, bounded work, hash/parse once; reviewers check query plans for new list queries.
policy-before-code: Owner 2026-11-06 strict rule: any behaviour change gets its docs/policy baseline written or updated and shown before the first code edit or writer brief.
policy-is-the-spec: Owner 2026-10-02: when roles, access or behaviour are already defined in docs/policy, implement from policy without asking the owner to approve a restatement or matrix. Ask only when policy is genuinely silent or contradictory, and then one plain question.
private-folder: private/ (gitignored) holds the owner's working material: WHO ICD-11/DORIS technical notes (20,010-certificate parity run 2026-10-29), architecture note, phone test plan, pptx, icd11-offline-spike/, engine-measurements/<date>-*, emulator-test-accounts.md, staging-ssm.md. Look there before writing WHO notes, parity evidence or benchmarks. It also holds keys/credentials: read only what you need, never copy secrets out.
research-data-never-committed: Owner 2026-11-05: data from real cases (dev DB payloads, server SmartVA results, sids, per-case replies) is research data: never commit it. Corpus, per-case outputs and mismatches stay in private/; committed results hold only aggregate counts, latencies, versions, sha256s. Synthetic sets (scripts/icd11-parity datasets) are fine.
reviewer-release-keeps-step1: Owner 2026-10-05: a reviewer releasing a started review keeps their saved Step 1 (same as timeout today); only reviewer NQA/review and social-autopsy analysis are cleared. Policy text 'all intermediate artifacts disappear' is corrected to match.
screen-widths: Owner 2026-11-04: users are on phones, tablets and 14-inch laptops; the owner's 4K whitespace is not the target. Check every changed web screen at ~375, 768 and ~1366 px (resize_window) before reporting it verified; say which widths were not checked.
single-test-runner: Owner 2026-10-14: one test runner agent per session, kept alive via SendMessage; never two runs on the same base test database (a parallel run caused a 30 s idle-in-transaction timeout). Writers run only targeted tests on their own minerva_test_<name>. Full backend suite is pytest -n 4 (~8 min, per-worker <base>_gwN).
staging-expo-export-build: Staging/production never build the Expo web export (2026-10-22): the app image's expo_web stage downloads the DigitVA release pinned in x-release-pins (EXPO_WEB_TAG, EXPO_WEB_SHA256) in docker-compose.yml, verifies SHA-256, installs to /opt/digitva/expo-client (EXPO_CLIENT_DIST); a normal image rebuild picks it up. Dev serves its local npm run export:web build (override file). To publish: build locally, tar dist contents, gh release create with .sha256, bump the two pins. Hindi xlf restore is a no-op when live matches (compare export-xliff first).
stopped-pytest-keeps-running: Stopping a background docker compose exec pytest kills only the client; the in-container pytest keeps using <db>_gw* and the next run dies with KeyError WorkerController / 'no tests ran' (exit 0). After stopping, docker compose exec -T minerva_app_service sh -c 'ps -eo pid,etimes,args | grep "[p]ytest"' and kill stale ones. 'no tests ran' is never a pass.
test-405-ban-shared-ip: Route tests that POST to GET-only routes (expecting 405) count toward the method-not-allowed IP ban on the shared test IP 127.0.0.1, stored in dev Redis under digitva_cache:digitva_test_method_not_allowed:ban:127.0.0.1 (1h). After a few runs every test-client request gets 403. Isolate such tests with a per-test METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED_BAN_PREFIX/COUNTER_PREFIX (see tests/test_request_method_abuse_control.py setUp).
vendor-package-owner-owns: Owner 2026-10-20: vendor/who-va-2022 is a plain directory (only vendor/smartva-analyze is a submodule) and the owner owns @drguptavivek/who-2022-va. Edit it freely, add vitest tests, commit with the app. npm run vendor:build rewrites package-lock.json (revert that); dist is gitignored.
web-intake-attachment-rows-must-keep-exi: Web-intake attachment rows must keep exists_on_odk=True: resolve_attachment_record only resolves rows with that flag; for web forms it means 'live', not 'came from Central'.
who-icd11-offline-permission: WHO correspondence and the owner's publishing rule are recorded in docs/policy/icd11-local-api-runtime.md ('WHO correspondence on offline use'). Summary: WHO (2026-10-26 reply, 2026-10-29 call) welcomes Android support, asked for the solution and a write-up, concerned about maintenance across releases; no written confirmation of licence 2.3/2.4 yet. Owner 2026-10-29: engine bundles (existing and new) may be public release assets ONLY if every input is public, open and unrestricted (WHO assemblies from the public whoicd/icd-api image by digest, WHO data from WHO's public CDN/storage by SHA-256, DigitVA bridge sources from the repo). The write-up says the bundle is public and still asks WHO for written confirmation of 2.3/2.4 and of data-file redistribution.
wunderbaum-browser-events: Browser checks on Wunderbaum trees: the browser pane's screenshot frame is not the page's coordinate frame, so drive Wunderbaum by dispatching events on elements, not by pixel clicks.
